extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors in K-12 and higher education; educators and adopters seeking open educational resources for beginning algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Features and quality criteria describing what a beginning-algebra textbook should provide: real-life/contextual problems, active/conceptual learning, problem-set design, group-work support, accessible electronic format, and licensing for educational reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of everyday contexts to teach algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the needs of learners to make sense of algebra by quantifying and generalizing everyday occurrences such as commuting to work, buying gas or pizza, and determining the better deal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present algebraic ideas through realistic, familiar scenarios so learners can relate symbolic work to daily-life decision-making and comparison tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active engagement via physical and thought experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires learners to actively engage with algebraic concepts through physical and thought experiments in ways that help them connect ideas, representations, and contexts, and solve problems that arise in their daily lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities and experiments (hands-on or mental) that prompt students to explore and discover algebraic structure, make connections between multiple representations, and apply reasoning to practical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual learning and growth mindset development
rubrics_metrics.description: Helps learners grow their brains and develop growth mindsets as they learn algebra conceptually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize understanding over rote procedures; incorporate language and tasks that promote persistence, improvement, and metacognitive reflection about learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem sets that extend and apply lesson content
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem sets continue the process, extending work begun in each lesson, applying new understandings to new contexts, and considering ideas that arise more fully in upcoming lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design problem sets to reinforce lesson concepts, include transfer tasks that place ideas in novel contexts, and scaffold toward deeper exploration covered later in the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer assignments suitable for group projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer assignments that can be used as group projects are included in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multi-part or open-ended tasks that require collaboration, project planning, and integration of concepts across lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and orchestration guidance for group work
rubrics_metrics.description: Group work is encouraged throughout the text; suggestions for orchestrating group work are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instructional notes or teacher guidance on how to organize, monitor, and assess group activities to maximize participation and learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible electronic format with rich media
rubrics_metrics.description: The text is open access and free for download by students and instructors in .pdf format. In the electronic format, graphics are in full color and there are live html links to resources, software, and applets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide downloadable, printable files and enrich electronic versions with full-color figures and clickable links to supplemental digital tools and applets to support exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open licensing with limited commercial permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-Share Alike 4.0 International License. In addition to the permissions granted by the CC-BY-NC-SA license, the author grants permission for bookstores and/or print shops at K-12, colleges, and universities to reproduce and sell print copies of this book. Other commercial uses of the book are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing should permit free student/instructor access and educational printing while restricting broader commercial exploitation; state clearly any additional permissions for institutional print reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted suitability for remedial and multiple education levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords and description indicate applicability to remedial mathematics and multiple levels: Middle School, High School, College/University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content, pacing, and supports (scaffolding, examples) to be usable across middle-school through college remedial contexts, with adaptability for different classroom levels.
